| [THEORY-026](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-026.md) v5 | Only nonpredictive memory wastes driven work | Still, Sivak, Bell & Crooks (2012), [LIT-327](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-327.md): β⟨W_diss⟩ for the switch x_t → x_{t+1} equals I[s_t;x_t] − I[s_t;x_{t+1}] (Eq. 14, an identity). | [THEORY-030](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-030.md) v4 | Landauer prices only losing distinguishability | Bennett (2003), [LIT-360](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-360.md): the cost attaches to many-to-one maps of the logical state, at least k ln 2 of entropy per bit exported to non-information-bearing degrees of freedom, which "need not" be heat. | [THEORY-072](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-072.md) v5 | Organisms differ from flames by differentiation | The record's first answer to the demarcation question that [NOTE-094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-094.md) reports. Prigogine ([LIT-516](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-516.md)) supplies the dissipative structures, and nothing in his account separates them from organisms. Mossio, Saborido & Moreno (2009, [LIT-570](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-570.md)) grant a candle flame organisational closure. Its one macroscopic pattern keeps up the conditions of the combustion that makes it. They draw the line at organisational differentiation: in an organism several distinct structures make distinct contributions, where a flame makes "a unique contribution". Montévil & Mossio (2015, [LIT-582](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-582.md)) narrow closure to mutual dependence among constraints. Each constraint must be both produced by and productive of another, with at least one slow and one fast dependence. On the record's reading, that builds differentiation into closure, as Mossio and Bich (2014) already say of closure of constraints. No paper analyses a flame under the 2015 definitions. Neither paper says closure defines an organism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-209.md) v2 | Converged SGD samples a modified Gibbs law | Kunin et al. (2021), [LIT-1011](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1011.md), read in [NOTE-711](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-711.md). Modelled as an underdamped Langevin equation with noise covariance proportional to the Hessian, SGD at the end of training converges to a nonequilibrium stationary state: Gibbs on a modified loss whose curvature undoes the Hessian's anisotropy, with inverse temperature S(1 − β²), in broken detailed balance. A ResNet-18 on ImageNet explores isotropically in a plane where the loss is anisotropic, oscillates at Hessian-dependent rates, and moves at the predicted speed across a hyperparameter sweep. For the learned-structure line, a trained solution is in part a property of the regime that trained it. Proposed: the deep-learning evidence is one network, under assumptions the paper concedes are strained. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md) v5 | SGD noise equalizes noise across symmetric groups | Ziyin, Li & Ueda ([LIT-1012](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1012.md), read in [NOTE-714](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-714.md)), with the gradient flow conservation law and the Itô term from Neural Mechanics ([LIT-1013](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1013.md)). If ℓ(u, w) = ℓ(λu, w/λ) for every sample, then under the SDE model of SGD d(‖u‖² − ‖w‖²)/dt = −T(uᵀC₁u − wᵀC₂w), with T = η/S. The noise has no component along the symmetry, but its dependence on the parameters produces a deterministic drift through Itô's lemma. The drift points to the noise-balanced point, and weight decay adds to its rate. In a diagonal linear network the stationary distribution follows exactly: it is non-ergodic, has a memory of initialization, and collapses to zero above a critical temperature. The law is re-derived here (2026-10-19) within the SDE model; the tests are small synthetic networks, and whether it holds in deep networks on real data is QUESTION-164. | Active |
| [THEORY-220](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-220.md) v5 | Self-maintenance grounds intrinsic function | Bickhard (2000), [LIT-1029](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1029.md), read in [NOTE-729](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-729.md). Function is contribution to a far-from-equilibrium system's own persistence; the asymmetry between persisting and decaying gives function and dysfunction, always relative to the system served, so a parasite's gut serves the parasite and harms the host. A candle flame has functions in this sense. Representation arrives with recursive self-maintenance: a system that picks its next interaction by how it has differentiated its environment implicitly predicates that the interaction will succeed, and can find the predication false. Proposed: a conceptual account, with no model, whose account of having a function (and so of malfunction) is deferred to another paper. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-275](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-275.md) v8 | Information flow follows drive, not coupling | Das, Manikandan and Banerjee (2025), [LIT-947](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-947.md), read in [NOTE-788](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-788.md). Two colloids are coupled by the fluid through a symmetric tensor, and recorded noise moves one trap. Time-delayed mutual information and transfer entropy give drive → driven → other, with backflow at moderate drive. In numerics only, flow is one-way at strong drive. With no drive the coupled particles are independent at steady state. The paper does not test an unrecorded drive shared by both units, and it does not claim that the measures reveal coupling architecture. Whether the same holds in other reciprocally coupled systems is QUESTION-186. | Active |
| [THEORY-412](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-412.md) v2 | Driven matter looks adapted without replication | Perunov, Marsland & England (2014; Phys. Rev. X 2016), [LIT-518](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-518.md), read in [NOTE-416](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-416.md), on England's macrostate relation ([LIT-515](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-515.md)). The log-odds of two driven outcomes decompose exactly into an internal-entropy term, a reversal term and Ψ − Φ = −ln⟨e^{−βΔQ}⟩. The "tendency towards adaptation" needs the first two held equal. | [THEORY-416](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-416.md) | Quantum work has four inequivalent notions | Vinjanampathy & Anders (2015/16), [LIT-010](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-010.md), read in full in [NOTE-011](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-011.md). The review's one synthesis (§5.2, §7) sets four definitions side by side: ⟨W⟩ = ∫tr[ρḢ]dt (Eq. 2), W = E_m^(τ) − E_n^(0) (Eq. 24), A^ε ≈ −kT ln(Z_Λ*/Z) (Eq. 49) and w^max_ε = F^min_ε(ρ_S) − F(τ_S) (Eq. 50). Only the last two agree, and that agreement is an observation that two published formulas match, for states diagonal in energy. It is an informed judgement of a 2016 snapshot, not a theorem that the notions cannot be unified. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-431](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-431.md) v2 | Crooks symmetry holds for entropy production | Crooks (1999), [LIT-522](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-522.md), read in [NOTE-413](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-413.md), with Jarzynski (1997), [LIT-517](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-517.md) ([NOTE-417](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-417.md)), and Seifert's review (2012), [LIT-523](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-523.md) ([NOTE-420](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-420.md)). The work equality ⟨e^{−βW}⟩ = e^{−βΔF} holds at any switching rate, and Crooks derives it from a trajectory-level entropy-production theorem; Seifert derives every known theorem of the kind from one master theorem. These are exact given their premises. They are not proofs of the second law, since the dynamics build irreversibility in, and they say nothing about extremum principles for steady states. Their practical reach is work fluctuations of order k_BT. | Active |
| [THEORY-463](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-463.md) | Dynamics alone can't give strict irreversibility | Frigg & Werndl (2023), [LIT-114](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-114.md), the SEP entry, read in [NOTE-103](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-103.md). | [THEORY-482](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-482.md) | Two-point work obeys classical fluctuation laws | Vinjanampathy & Anders (2015/16), [LIT-010](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-010.md), read in full in [NOTE-011](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-011.md), which reproduces the derivation (Eqs. 24–30). With W_{m,n} = E_m^(τ) − E_n^(0), a thermal start and closed unitary evolution, ⟨e^{−βW}⟩ = e^{−βΔF} follows from Σ_n p_{m\|n} = 1 (Eq. 29), identical in form to the classical relation. It says nothing about work defined without them. | Active |

| [THEORY-517](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-517.md) | Life raises Earth's entropy production | Kleidon (2009), [LIT-519](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-519.md), read in [NOTE-423](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-423.md). | [THEORY-532](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-532.md) | Life degrades applied gradients faster | Schneider & Kay (1994), [LIT-533](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-533.md), read in [NOTE-415](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-415.md). | [THEORY-679](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-679.md) v2 | Replication heat grows with durability, not info | England (2012; J. Chem. Phys. 2013), [LIT-515](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-515.md), read in [NOTE-419](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-419.md). The general bound, β⟨ΔQ⟩ + ln π(II→I) + ΔS_int ≥ 0, is a coarse-grained second law and was re-derived. Applied to replication it gives a heat cost of about 2n ln(n τ_decay/τ_div) per copy, which falls away as division slows. The numbers for E. coli (within a factor of three of the bound) and RNA rest on an upper bound on the reverse probability that is argued from biology, not proved, and on an internal-entropy term set "arbitrarily". It prices finite-time irreversibility, not information, and draws no line between living and non-living replicators. | Active |
| [THEORY-692](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-692.md) | Far from equilibrium, fluctuations can grow | Prigogine (1977), [LIT-516](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-516.md), read in full in [NOTE-424](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-424.md), with Cross & Hohenberg (1993), [LIT-527](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-527.md), skimmed in [NOTE-418](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-418.md). Minimum entropy production holds only for steady states in the strictly linear regime with constant coefficients. Beyond it, non-negative excess entropy production suffices for stability; its failure is not shown to give instability. Which structure appears is left to kinetics, boundaries and fluctuations. Cross and Hohenberg find no global minimisation principle beyond a perturbative one near threshold, and quote Glansdorff and Prigogine conceding that "the search for a universal kinetic potential has proved to be unsuccessful". | Active |

| [THEORY-1270](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1270.md) | Entropy production doesn't select stable states | Vellela & Qian (2009), [LIT-1890](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1890.md) (§3.3, Fig. 6), read in [NOTE-1474](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1474.md), show the counterexample; Falasco & Esposito (2025), [LIT-1892](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1892.md) (§§III.F, IV.H, VIII.B.6), read in [NOTE-1472](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1472.md), give the general account: minimum entropy production holds only near detailed balance with linear dynamics, and the two maximum principles hold only where relaxation and escape dissipations nearly coincide. Active as a negative result. It does not refute every extremum principle, only those that rank steady states by dissipation alone. | Active |
| [THEORY-1273](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1273.md) v3 | Bistable chemical states are metastable | Vellela & Qian (2009), [LIT-1890](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1890.md), read in [NOTE-1474](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1474.md), on the Schlögl model, with Falasco & Esposito's general frame ([LIT-1892](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1892.md), §§III.C, IV.H, VI; [NOTE-1472](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1472.md)). Active: the slow eigenvalue, the barriers, the initial-condition independence and the closing of the barrier at the fold were checked numerically on the paper's model. It does not say which state is the more stable without computing the quasi-potential, and the paper's own large-volume rate formula carries a spurious 1/V factor. | Active |
| [THEORY-1437](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1437.md) v3 | Origami staples bind fully once started | Cumberworth and Reinhardt (2025), [LIT-2121](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2121.md), read in full in [NOTE-1626](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1626.md) from the submitted version. Active as a report of the review's synthesis of coarse-grained simulations, mostly the authors' own, of small 2D designs. The authors note evidence that staples do not bind fully once started in a larger 3D-lattice-based design, and that their lattice model's loop costs are fixed only up to a constant. The experimental evidence on origami hysteresis they report is mixed. Whether experiment bears the account out is [QUESTION-445](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-445.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1448](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1448.md) v2 | Templating raises tile sticky-end concentration | Ni, Zhou, Zhu, Bershadsky, Ai, Wang, Sha, Seeman and Chaikin (2026), [LIT-2124](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2124.md), read in [NOTE-1630](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1630.md). The effective-concentration figure is the model's estimate, with a FRET fit of about 0.2 mM; the 2 °C agreement is over assemblies up to tetramers; the replication rates are one figure whose definition is in a supplementary figure not read. The paper's predicted upper limit on string melting temperature, and with it the feasibility of replicating very large patterns, is extrapolation; in experiment tetramers barely separated before the tiles unravelled. | Active |
| [THEORY-1453](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1453.md) v2 | Origami nucleation barrier set by stacking | Cumberworth, Frenkel and Reinhardt (2022), [LIT-2134](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2134.md), read in [NOTE-1638](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1638.md). Equilibrium simulation of four designs of at most 27 domains with averaged energies. It does not say that a barrier changes folding times or yields, which are not simulated, nor that it causes the hysteresis seen in temperature ramps, which the authors explain but do not reproduce, nor that larger designs have no other barriers. | Active |
| [THEORY-1454](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1454.md) v2 | Anchored folds are stabler; distance costs | Majikes, Patrone, Schiffels, Zwolak, Kearsley, Forry and Liddle (2020), [LIT-2117](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2117.md), read in [NOTE-1632](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1632.md) (main text, captions and tables; the supplement unread). Active as a report; its limits: one fold and one melt domain, measured on the melt only, with equilibrium assumed and not tested. The title asserts the measurement and that the authors infer the pathway; it does not assert the pathway, which the authors say needs systems with multiple folds, nor anything about hysteresis, kinetics or whole-origami yield. | Active |
| [THEORY-1457](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1457.md) v2 | Excess staples block folds past a turnover | Majikes, Patrone, Kearsley, Zwolak and Liddle (2021), [LIT-2133](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2133.md), read in [NOTE-1633](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1633.md) (main text, captions and tables; the supplement, with the slower-anneal control, unread). Active as a report; its limits: one lab, one fold at a time, one reporter channel that cannot tell blocked from unbound, and one fold distance declared anomalous by assumption. The title asserts the single-fold measurement and that the authors propose the whole-origami escape; it does not assert the escape, nor that the blocked state is a kinetic trap. | Active |
| [THEORY-1646](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1646.md) | Semantic information is what viability needs |  | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1830](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1830.md) | Biochemical function needs dissipation | Tu (2026), [LIT-2547](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2547.md), read in [NOTE-1904](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1904.md). The derivations are in small Markov networks: a three-state proofreading model, a four-state "magic square", and a mean-field model of coupled Poisson clocks. The sharp edges: the ESA relation is leading-order, and in the filer's check accuracy saturates at a residual set by the network's own parameters, past which more dissipation buys speed and no accuracy; and the proposed law, Ẇ ≥ F(P₁, P₂, …) with F unspecified, is a schema whose content lies only in its instances. | Active |
| [THEORY-2011](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2011.md) | Least-dissipation memory is an info bottleneck | From the reading of [LIT-2832](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2832.md) in [NOTE-2097](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2097.md). Still (arXiv 1705.00612, 2017; Physical Review Letters 124, 050601, 2020). The letter extends Szilárd's engine to partial observability and two temperatures. Forming a memory costs at least kT·I[M,X], and extracting work recovers at most kT'·I[M,Y], where Y is what the extraction device can manipulate. Minimising the resulting dissipation bound over the memory map is exactly the information bottleneck, with the temperature ratio as its trade-off. The agent's action never changes the next cycle's data, so the result is a no-feedback baseline. Here because the exchange made it the bridge between memory and thermodynamics: it is the nearest prior result for [QUESTION-494](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-494.md) and extends [THEORY-026](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-026.md) to a cyclic engine. Read in its NOTE (arXiv v3). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2176](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2176.md) | Gamma superstatistics gives Tsallis statistics | Beck and Cohen (2003), [LIT-2962](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2962.md), read in [NOTE-2265](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2265.md). A letter: the mixture-of-exponentials construction in physics, with a gamma density giving the Tsallis form exactly and a universality result at small variance. It never says "power law"; which densities give one is the assistant's [CLAIM-857](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-857.md). Proposed until the published text or a second source confirms it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2194](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2194.md) | No magnetic order in D ≤ 2 Heisenberg models | Gelfert and Nolting (2001), [LIT-3057](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3057.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2290](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2290.md) as a stand-in for Mermin and Wagner (1966), [LIT-2985](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2985.md). The proof's outline and the graph version are both at second hand: the bounds are stated "as has been shown by Mermin and Wagner", and Cassi's theorem is reported in one paragraph. It is the record's ground for [CLAIM-842](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-842.md)'s d_s ≤ 2 criterion as a theorem of spin models ([ARG-200](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-200.md)). Proposed until the originals are read. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2196](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2196.md) | Every current obeys the uncertainty relation | Gingrich and colleagues (2016), [LIT-2981](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2981.md), read in [NOTE-2291](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2291.md). The general proof of the thermodynamic uncertainty relation that Barato and Seifert ([LIT-1885](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1885.md), [THEORY-1268](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1268.md)) proved only in linear response and for unicyclic networks and otherwise conjectured: for every current of a Markov jump network, far from equilibrium included, and as a bound on the whole rate function, so on rare fluctuations as well as the variance. Long-time, steady-state, reversible transitions only. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2197](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2197.md) | 2D XY low-T phase is critical throughout | Drouin-Touchette (2022), [LIT-3055](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3055.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2295](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2295.md) as a stand-in for Kosterlitz and Thouless (1973), [LIT-2969](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2969.md). Standard results, derived at a student level and credited to Kosterlitz (1974) and José et al. (1977). Grounds [CLAIM-841](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-841.md)'s XY row with Kosterlitz's lecture ([THEORY-2206](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2206.md)) ([ARG-198](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-198.md)), and the BKT case of [CLAIM-862](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-862.md). Proposed until checked against the primary papers. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2203](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2203.md) | Mermin–Wagner forbids only true long-range order | Halperin (2018), [LIT-3054](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3054.md), read in full in [NOTE-2296](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2296.md) as a stand-in for Mermin and Wagner (1966), [LIT-2985](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2985.md). The theorem's scope and its exceptions, as an author close to it states them. Marks the limits of [CLAIM-842](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-842.md)'s criterion ([ARG-200](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-200.md)), and why [CLAIM-841](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-841.md)'s XY row does not rest on Mermin–Wagner. Proposed until a second source confirms the scope. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2205](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2205.md) | Macrostates are causal states of observables | Shalizi and Moore (2003), [LIT-2996](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2996.md), read in [NOTE-2294](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2294.md). Their answer to whether macrostates are objective or subjective is "both": the observables are the observer's, the causal states reached from them are fixed by the dynamics. "A different set of initial variables will, generally, lead to a different set of causal states"; "Nature has no preferred questions." Their emergence is a coarse-graining predicted more efficiently (argon: 0.87 against 0.5), held in [TERM-146](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-146.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2206](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2206.md) | 2D rotors have a topological ordered phase | Kosterlitz (2016), [LIT-3053](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3053.md), read in full in [NOTE-2283](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2283.md) as a stand-in for Kosterlitz and Thouless (1973), [LIT-2969](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2969.md). The first author's restatement, with the 1973 paper's errors named. It grounds [CLAIM-841](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-841.md)'s XY row with Drouin-Touchette ([THEORY-2197](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2197.md)) ([ARG-198](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-198.md)); it gives [CLAIM-694](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-694.md) the barrier condition; and it is one case of [CLAIM-862](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-862.md). Proposed until the primary papers are read. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2278](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2278.md) | Staple folding is cooperative in DNA origami | In "small origamis" of one 64-base scaffold and two staples, a staple's melting peak rises when the other is folded (48.5 to 51.5 °C outer, 41.5 to 50 °C inner, 67 to 72 °C and +1.5 °C for a second pair), and the inner position, where the path between a crossover's ends runs through the staple, costs more than the bulge-forming outer one. A model of local equilibria conditioned on bound neighbours, with a strong-correlation closure and no misfolds or kinetics, fits the annealing and melting curves and the hysteresis (4 to 10 K) of four rectangular M13 origamis. | Proposed |
